Describe the shaded region shown above using set-builder notation.

$$
{(x,y)\in {{field-1}}\,:\,2x\,{{field-2}}\,y\,{{field-3}}\,-x+3}
$$
q-181685.worked_solution:
The points in our set include all those that lie *above* the line $y=2x$ and *below* the line $y=-x+3.$

A point $P(x,y)$ lies *inside* the shaded region if the following conditions are satisfied:

$$
y>2x,\,y<-x+3.
$$

 

Combining this into a single condition, we have

$$
2x<y<-x+3.
$$

 

Since the boundary is not included in the set (the lines are dashed), the inequalities are strict.

Moreover, since we're considering *every* real value in this region, $x\in R,y\in R,$ and therefore 

$$
(x,y)\in R\times R={R}^{2}.
$$

Therefore, we can write the set as

$$
{(x,y)\in {R}^{2}\,:\,2x<y<-x+3}.
$$

q-181688.worked_solution:
The points in our set include all those that lie *above* the line $y=x+1$ and *below* the line $y=3x.$

A point $P(x,y)$ lies *inside* the shaded region if the following conditions are satisfied:

$$
y>x+1,\,y<3x.
$$

Combining this into a single condition, we have

$$
x+1<y<3x.
$$

We must also include the line $y=3x$ since the boundary is included in the set (the curve is solid). So, we change the corresponding inequality symbol above as follows:

$$
x+1<y\le 3x
$$

Moreover, since we're considering *every* real value in this region, $x\in R,y\in R,$ and therefore 

$$
(x,y)\in R\times R={R}^{2}.
$$

Therefore, we can write the set as

$$
{(x,y)\in {R}^{2}\,:\,x+1<y\le 3x}.
$$

q-181810.worked_solution:
The equation of an ellipse centered at the origin with a horizontal radius of length $a$ and a vertical radius of length $b$ is given by

$$
\frac{{x}^{2}}{{a}^{2}}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{{b}^{2}}=1.
$$

 

Here, the elliptical boundary of our region has horizontal radius $a=3$ and vertical radius $b=4.$ Therefore, the equation of the ellipse is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{x}^{2}}{9}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{16} & =1,\end{aligned}
$$

which we can write as

$$
16{x}^{2}+9{y}^{2}=144.
$$

We're interested in describing all points that lie *inside* the ellipse. So, let's pick any point inside the region, say, $(0,0).$ Substituting its coordinates into the equation of the boundary, we obtain

$$
16(0)^{2}+9(0)^{2}\,<\,144.
$$

As a result, the points $P(x,y)$ in our region are any real numbers that satisfy the condition

$$
16{x}^{2}+9{y}^{2}<144.
$$

Notice that we use $<$ since the boundary is excluded from the set (the boundary curve is dashed).

Therefore, we can write the set as

$$
{(x,y)\in {R}^{2}\,:\,16{x}^{2}+9{y}^{2}<144}.
$$

Therefore, a point $P(x,y)$ lies *inside* the shaded region if the following condition is satisfied:

$$
y>-x+1
$$

$$
y>-x+1.

$$
(x,y)\in R\times R={R}^{2}.
$$

$$
{(x,y)\in {R}^{2}\,:\,y>-x+1}.
$$

q-181999.worked_solution:
The points in our set include all those that lie *above* the line $y=2.$

Therefore, a point $P(x,y)$ lies *inside* the shaded region if the following condition is satisfied:

$$
y>2
$$

Since the boundary is *not* included in the set (the curve is *not* solid),  no further action must be taken, so we have

$$
y>2.
$$

Moreover, since we're considering *every* real value in this region, $x\in R,y\in R,$ and therefore 

$$
(x,y)\in R\times R={R}^{2}.
$$

Therefore, we can write the set as

$$
{(x,y)\in {R}^{2}\,:\,y>2}.
$$
